summary: Su Bai worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed graduate studies at Peking University (1940–1944) under Chengjun Feng, Zuoyun Sun, Rong Geng, and Yongtong Tang, and later served there as professor from 1948 to 2004.

Diskul studied at Chulalongkorn, École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and UCL/University of London. He was curator at Bangkok National Museum (~1953–1958), professor, dean, and rector at Silpakorn University (1964; 1976–1986), and director of SEAMEO SPAFA (~1986–1992).

Kak studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under Pavaguda V. Indiresan. An Indologist and engineer, he held posts at LSU from 1979 and became Regents Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Oklahoma State University in 2007.

Subrata K. Mitra studied at Utkal University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Rochester (~1973–1978). His academic posts include the University of Hull (~1980–1989), Heidelberg University (~1994–2014), and the National University of Singapore (2015–2018).

Sucheng Chan worked in history and archaeology, studying at Swarthmore College (~1959–1963), the University of Hawaiʻi (~1963–1965), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1969–1973). She later became emerita professor at UC Santa Barbara (~1984).

Kakar, active in religious studies and Indology, studied at Gujarat University, Mannheim, Vienna, and the Sigmund-Freud-Institut. He served as professor at IIM Ahmedabad (~1971–1977) and department head at IIT Delhi (1976–1977), alongside numerous international visiting posts.

An Indologist and historian of mathematics, Dvivedī studied under Devakrishna. At Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, he served as librarian (1883), professor of mathematics and astrology (1890), and head of the mathematics faculty (1898–1905).

Sue Hamilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, and later held a post at King's College London (attested 2001–2003).
Suehiro Tanemura studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957). He later held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1972–1984) and Kokugakuin University (~1984–1999).

Suk Fun Ng is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014). Her studies were supervised by Jing Yin and Y. Karunadasa, and she also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

Sanghvi studied at Shri Yashovijaya Jain Sanskrit Pathshala and under Balakrishna Mishra. Specializing in Indology and philosophy, he was professor of Indian philosophy at Gujarat Vidyapith (1922) and Chair of Jain Philosophy at Banaras Hindu University (1934–1944).

Sukra Sagar Shrestha worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts as an epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986) and the Department of Archaeology (attested 1987).

A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Sen studied at Burdwan Raj College, Sanskrit College, and Calcutta University under Suniti Kumar Chatterji and I. J. S. Taraporewala. He lectured at Calcutta University from 1930 and became Khaira Professor in 1954.

Sukumari Bhattacharji was an Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. She served as a professor of English at Lady Brabourne College (1945) and taught at Jadavpur University from 1957 to 1986.

Sulak Sivaraksa, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied at Lampeter (~1954–1958). He was editor for the Social Science Association of Thailand (~1963–1969) and held visiting professorships at Berkeley, Harvard, Toronto, and Cornell.

Sumathi Ramaswamy is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Delhi, JNU, and the University of Pennsylvania, and held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1993–1997) and the University of Michigan (~1997–2007).

Sumi Lee specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Alexander L. Mayer and earned a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles under Robert Buswell (attested 2014).

Katre, an Indologist and linguist, earned a Ph.D. from the University of London. He held the Chair of Indo-European Philology at Deccan College (1942–1971) and was a professor at the University of Texas at Austin (~1971–1976).

Sun-Ah Choi works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Juhyung Rhi, also studying under Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

Sung Bae Park studied under doctoral supervisor Lewis Lancaster in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was an assistant professor of Buddhist studies at Dongguk University and took up a post at Stony Brook University in 1977.
